subject: Audit log proofing and extract paths - Novomed evidence request
messages:
From: Audrey Lin <audrey.lin@novomed.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Audit log evidence request — admin activity & export paths

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this. Novomed's compliance team is preparing for an upcoming SIG/SOC2 review and we need a short deliverable that explains what admin/admin-activity/audit logs Redwood can provide. Specifically we need:

- A concise list of event types you record (examples: console sign-ins, API key create/rotate/delete, role/grant changes, model deployment actions, routing/fallback events, cache invalidations, export actions, KMS key usage) and the fields captured for each event.
- Default retention windows and any configurable retention tiers.
- Available export mechanisms (one-time snapshot, incremental cursor/delta, streaming SIEM connector, presigned S3 delivery, SFTP, signed manifest options).
- Format and attestations: do you provide a signed manifest (HMAC or PGP), checksums, and an auditable delivery chain-of-custody?
- Support for PII redaction or tenant scoping in exports (we will need tenant-scoped evidence for our SOC2 scope).

We'd like a 90-day sample export for immediate review and a plan for a full 12-month snapshot. Can you include an estimated turnaround and what artifacts you would attach (schema/README, checksums, example manifest)?

Thanks — please include Ben if there are any SLAs or procurement items to consider.

Regards,
Audrey Lin
Director, Compliance
Novomed

Attachment: novomed_evidence_request_form.pdf (pdf)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Audrey Lin <audrey.lin@novomed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-01T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Audit log evidence request — admin activity & export paths

Hi Audrey — thanks for the clear ask. Below is a concise summary we can hand to your auditor; I attached a compact CSV describing the admin-event schema and a short runbook for exports. We can produce the 90-day sample within 3 business days once we agree on the delivery target and scoping (tenant ID + time window).

What Redwood logs (representative event types and important fields):
- auth.sign_in: user_id, method (OIDC/SAML), ip, user_agent, success/failure, timestamp, session_id
- api_key.{create,rotate,delete}: actor_id, api_key_id (masked), operation, timestamp, requester_ip, request_id
- iam.role.{create,assign,revoke,delete}: actor_id, role_id, target_principal, before/after, timestamp
- deployment.{start,complete,rollback}: actor_id, model_id, model_version, instance_type, region, request_id, timestamp
- routing.fallback: route_id, trigger_reason (latency/oom/capacity), fallback_model, original_model, timestamp
- cache.invalidate: actor_id, cache_key_hash, scope (global/tenant), timestamp
- export.{initiate,complete,fail}: export_id, scope, time_range_start, time_range_end, delivery_method, manifest_checksum, signer
- kms.access: key_id (partial), actor_id, operation, timestamp (we log key usage metadata but do not expose raw key material)

Fields included: timestamp, event_id (UUID), tenant_id, actor_id (internal user/email/service), event_type, event_payload (JSON blob with structured details), request_id, source_ip, region. PII: account emails are recorded in actor_id but can be redacted in export per tenant-scoped requests (see redaction section).

Retention & tiers:
- Default retention (admin events): 365 days
- Extended retention options: up to 3 years via Reserved Evidence retention add-on (policy-controlled)
- Session traces / full request bodies: 90 days by default (longer retention available on signed enterprise agreements)
- Short-term backups for export window freeze: we keep a cryptographic snapshot for 30 days post-delivery for verification purposes

Export formats & delivery options:
- Snapshot tarball (JSONL per event type) + manifest.csv + checksums (SHA256). Tarball is encrypted with customer KMS key if requested.
- Incremental delta exports: cursor-based JSONL slices (useful for SIEM ingest).
- Streaming connectors: Splunk HTTP Event Collector, Sumo Logic, or Kafka (private peering).
- Direct delivery: presigned S3 (AWS), signed GCS URL (GCP), SFTP drop (customer endpoint).
- Transport attestations: option to include an HMAC-signed manifest (we sign using Redwood key; customers can request PGP/bring-your-key signing and we will include key metadata).

Chain-of-custody & attestations:
- Each export bundle includes manifest.csv describing files, event counts, SHA256 checksums, export_id, generated_by (redwood_operator_id), and a signature block.
- We optionally produce an HMAC (shared key) or PGP signature over the manifest. We also include a delivery log: who initiated, IP, timestamp, and delivery mechanism.

PII redaction & tenant scoping:
- Exports can be filtered by tenant_id to produce tenant-only evidence.
- Field-level redaction rules are configurable per request: replace email addresses and other sensitive fields with deterministic salted hashes or redact entirely.

Turnaround & artifacts:
- 90-day sample: 3 business days after scope confirmation and any required legal approvals.
- 12-month snapshot: 7–10 business days (depends on volume).
- Artifacts we attach: admin_event_schema_v3.csv (column mapping), export_runbook_v1.pdf (delivery steps), manifest example, checksums.txt.

Delivery & security notes:
- For presigned S3/GCS we recommend a minimum 168-hour expiry for large transfers; for SFTP we provide temporary credentials with IP allowlist.
- We support encrypting the bundle with your KMS key (provide key ARN/ID & IAM role).

Next steps:
1) Confirm scope (tenant ID + exact time range for the 90-day sample).
2) Confirm preferred delivery method (presigned S3 or SFTP) and a contact for credentials.
3) If you require signed manifests with your key, share the public key or KMS metadata.

I attached the schema and runbook. Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Attachments:
- admin_event_schema_v3.csv (csv)
- export_runbook_v1.pdf (pdf)

Quick follow-up — a couple of clarifications from our side that will help Novomed's auditor:

- Redaction modes: please confirm deterministic hashing uses a per-tenant salt and whether we can provide a salt rotation policy. (Auditors like to see how hashing prevents linkage across data sets.)
- Manifest signing: Audrey asked for HMAC/PGP options. If Novomed wants HMAC, we'll need to coordinate a shared key exchange; for PGP, please provide the public key. We should note whether Redwood retains the signing key or if customer-supplied keys are mandatory for an attested deliverable.
- KMS metadata: if Novomed requests bundle encryption, we must collect key ARN (AWS) or key resource name and a role ARN that Redwood will assume to write the encrypted object.

Soojin, I drafted a short paragraph about our attestation model for the manifest — want me to add it to the runbook before we send the sample?

-Kim
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

Thanks — this looks great. Novomed confirms:

- Scope: tenant_id=novomed-prod, 2028-02-01 through 2028-05-31 (90-day sample).
- Delivery: presigned S3 preferred; please encrypt the tarball with our KMS key (AWS ARN provided below via secure channel).
- Manifest: we request HMAC signature using a shared key (we will exchange via your secure key exchange process).

Procurement note: we will attach a PO after we receive the 90-day sample and manifest. If you could include a short README in the bundle describing any truncation/redaction rules applied, that would help auditors.

I'll expect the sample by EOD next Tuesday — let me know if Redwood needs anything else to start.

Best,
Audrey
